turns.learner: Oral calculus. For F(x) equal to the integral from 0 to x squared of 2t dt, I got F'(0)=0 by putting zero where I saw an x. I don't know if my rule would keep working. Give me a single test to do myself before explaining what happened.
turns.tutor:
For the same function
\[
F(x)=\int_0^{x^2}2t\,dt,
\]
find **\(F'(1)\)**. Show your reasoning so we can check whether your rule works beyond zero.

turns.learner: My rule was just twice the upper limit. What missing step changes that? Give one worked step and let me try again.
turns.tutor:
Your rule gives \(2x^2\), but it misses **how fast the upper limit changes**. Multiply by the derivative of \(x^2\):

\[
F'(x)=\underbrace{2x^2}_{\text{integrand at the upper limit}}
\underbrace{(2x)}_{\text{derivative of the upper limit}}.
\]

Now use this to find \(F'(1)\).
